newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO PROVIDE SUBSIDIES TO FIGHT UNEMPLOYMENT.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO PROVIDE SUBSIDIES TO FIGHT UNEMPLOYMENT.

text.p: A series of measures to fight unemployment and create 40,000 jobs, were announced by Labour and Social Security Minister Miltiades Papaioannou, the Athens News Agency (ANA) reported on Friday.
The measures include subsidies to employers as incentives to create new job openings. Subsidies will range from 2,500 to 5,000 drachmas per day for each worker and will last for 12 months.
A necessary condition for the successful implementation of the programme requires employers to keep employees on their books for at least an extra four months after the ensd of subsidisation.
Some 9,000 jobs will be created for those aged 15 to 25, 4,000 positions for women, 10,000 for those unemployed for a long time and 7,000 for those who were part of massive lay-offs, ANA said.

Another package will provide subsidies in the range of 900,000 to 1,400,000 drachmas for 10,000 unemployed people to enter self-employment, it added. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
